## Mesh-agree: a Mesh whose blocks disagree runs eager (no switch) {#sec-ch13-agree}

### Summary

The blocks of a Mesh capture together or not at all. If one block refuses capture (an outflow boundary, a solid
mask, a state not on the GPU) or the blocks' execution modes differ, every block of the Mesh runs eager. Without
this rule a capturing block would meet a refusing block's in-stage exchanges a different number of times and the
Mesh would hang (@sec-ch13-cuts).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** A block captures only if every other block of its Mesh has the same resolved execution mode and no
refusal reason; otherwise it gets the reason "a Mesh whose blocks disagree" and runs eager.

**Data.** In: each block's resolved mode, its configuration reasons (live) and its variables' reasons (as of the
last `agree`). Out: a refusal reason per block.

**Placement.** Before every stage of a Mesh (`MeshImpl::forward` calls `agree`), and at `Mesh::initialize`.

**Activation.** Always on for a Mesh of more than one block; no switch.

**Guarantee / limits.** A disagreeing Mesh runs eager as a whole; under `execution_strict` it is refused before
its first launch.

**Evidence.** @sec-ch13-agree-tests.
:::

The rule compares the blocks' resolved modes (`StageExecutor::mode`), not the deck key; `agree` only refreshes
each block's variable reasons, and the comparison is in `capture_reasons`.

### Derivation

No equation: a rule. For blocks $b \ne b'$ of one Mesh, block $b$ may capture only if
$\mathrm{mode}(b') = \mathrm{mode}(b)$ and block $b'$ has no configuration or variable reason, for every $b'$. The
first $b'$ that fails either test gives block $b$ its reason, naming $b'$ and either the two modes or $b'$'s first
reason. The rule is symmetric in effect: if any block refuses, every block gets a reason.

### Numerical method

`agree` records each block's variable reasons (state not on a CUDA device, a solid mask set) from the variables the
caller passes. `capture_reasons` of a block starts from its own variable and configuration reasons; if it has none
and the Mesh has more than one block, it walks the other blocks, comparing modes first and then their
configuration reasons (computed live) and recorded variable reasons. A non-empty list sends the block's stage down
the eager path. @fig-ch13-mesh-agree shows the decision.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch13-mesh-agree
#| fig-cap: "The Mesh-agree decision for one block of a three-block Mesh. Left: all blocks share a mode and none refuses, so each block captures. Right: block 2 refuses (an outflow boundary), so blocks 0 and 1 get the reason 'a Mesh whose blocks disagree' and the whole Mesh runs eager."
#| fig-alt: "Two panels of three boxes each; in the left panel all boxes are marked graph, in the right panel one box is marked refuses and all three are marked eager."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch13.figures.fig_mesh_agree import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| record variable reasons | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::agree >}} | `agree` | none |
| variable reasons | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::vars_reasons >}} | `vars_reasons` | none |
| the rule | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::capture_reasons >}} | `capture_reasons` | none |
| configuration reasons | {{< code src/mesh/stage_executor.cpp StageExecutor::config_reasons >}} | `config_reasons` | `execution` |
| called before a stage | {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}} | `forward` | none |

Walk-through: `MeshImpl::forward` calls `agree(vars)`, then `check_strict` on each block (which raises for a strict
block that cannot capture), then `align_captures` and the stage. The reason a block runs eager is in its
execution report and capability rows.

### Tests {#sec-ch13-agree-tests}

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_mesh_disagree.cpp` (`test_mesh_disagree.release`) | one refusing block (an outflow boundary) makes the other block name "a Mesh whose blocks disagree", nothing captures, and the Mesh equals an eager Mesh; a strict Mesh whose blocks disagree is refused with that reason; blocks whose modes differ run eager | exact (`torch::equal`) | the test source |

Evidence: it passed in a by-name ctest subset on a CUDA build before the pin;[^agree-subset] not run at the pin
itself (missing evidence there). One process.

[^agree-subset]: [sha: 1b12ea5dc7eb71c89f07256d10cf379c20defe20] `ctest -j 1 -R 'rendezvous|capture|seam|cubed|mesh|block_job'`,
    CUDA build, 58 of 58 passed, one CUDA device (sm_61).

### Limits

The rule makes a whole Mesh eager for one block's reason, so a deck with one refusing block loses capture
everywhere; the reason is reported, not fixed. The variable reasons of the other blocks are as of the last `agree`,
which `Mesh::initialize` and every `Mesh::forward` call. Switch combinations are in @sec-ch12-matrix.
